page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon CPU with 4 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The CPU and system memory subsystems perform in the bottom 25% tier, as evidenced by weak stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block transfers registering at 26.07 GB/sec. However, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in the top 10% for large language model inference. Prompt processing and text generation for both small 135M and medium 7B models achieve high throughput, such as 2296.42 tokens per second for 7B prompt processing and 52.18 tokens per second for 7B text generation.

The primary tradeoff of the g2-standard-4 is its modest CPU and memory performance relative to its highly capable GPU. This makes it a highly cost-efficient option for workloads that offload the majority of their computational weight to the GPU, such as small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning deployment, and graphics rendering, while avoiding the higher costs associated with larger CPU allocations. Conversely, it is less suited for CPU-heavy tasks, database operations, or high-throughput local storage processing due to the lack of local storage and lower CPU benchmarks.
